statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail sits well below the block threshold while overnight price discovery stays contained after Monday's record close.
recommendation: Overnight structure is orderly: NQ futures hold a narrow ~0.45% range with retracements available, so no persistent one-way path is observed. Conditional trend-up risk concentrates in the Tuesday US cash session and is expressed as a narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC danger window rather than a broad session-wide restriction.
headline: Contained overnight range after Monday's record chip-led close; Tail low with a narrow Tuesday US-session protective band
body: Monday delivered a record Nasdaq-100 close at 30,482.35 (+2.83%, +838 points), with the Nasdaq Composite also closing at a record and the S&P 500 up about 1.5%. The catalyst was a repricing of CPU demand after Meta unveiled its Muse AI agent, lifting Arm about 13%, Intel about 12%, AMD about 9% to a record above $610 and a brief $1 trillion market value, and Qualcomm roughly 9%; the PHLX Semiconductor Index rose just over 3%, confirming the move was CPU-specific rather than a broad chip melt-up. NDX closed near, but not at, the session high of 30,557.33 and remains about 1% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20. Overnight, NQ futures trade near 30,898 (+0.37%) inside a roughly 138-point range (about 0.45%), which is contained two-way price discovery rather than persistent extension. Cross-asset confirmation is only partial: VIX is near 14.87 with a narrow 14.60-15.13 range, the 10-year yield eased about 4 basis points to roughly 4.96% and the 2-year was unchanged near 4.75%, so yields are not aligned with an equity squeeze. Oil is recovering modestly, with WTI near $93 (+0.8%) and Brent near $101 (+0.9%) after a four-session slide driven by hopes of US-Iran diplomacy at the UN General Assembly, which opens Tuesday, and by signs of recovering Saudi exports after drone damage closed the East-West pipeline. That conflict is unresolved and remains a genuine two-sided discontinuity mechanism: further de-escalation would feed the existing up-trend, while a reversal would risk violent directional repricing. The Federal Reserve raised rates at its September 15-16 meeting and left further increases open, so this week's speaker sequence carries weight even though no Tier-1 US release is scheduled before Wednesday's flash PMI. Taken together, a record close near 52-week highs with a live thematic catalyst is the configuration most capable of producing the shallow-pullback path that overwhelms mean reversion, but none of that structure is observed yet, so current Tail stays in the low band with the conditional risk placed in the US session.

lookbackSummary: Past 24h: Monday's US session ran a chip-led trend-up regime that lifted Tail from single digits in the Asian hours to an intraday peak of 33 around 19:00 UTC, with Stress reaching 57 and the mapped policy state passing through yellow into orange between 14:00 and 19:00 UTC. The regime then decayed in an orderly way into the close, Tail falling to 23 by 20:00 UTC and 14 by 21:00 UTC, which is the signature of a trend day that still permitted retracement rather than a no-retracement path. The last five hours have been a stable green overnight base with Tail easing from 13 to 11, Stress in the low-30s and Confidence high throughout.
outlookSummary: Base case is a calm overnight continuation with Tail in the low band and mode normal. The forecast tilts conditionally trend-up through the European session and into the Tuesday US cash open at 13:30 UTC, entering the watch band from 13:00 UTC and peaking at a narrow protective band between 15:00 and 17:00 UTC, which defines the danger window. That band assumes a scenario of opening continuation with shallow pullbacks toward the 30,762 52-week high; it is protective rather than observed and reverts quickly if orderly retracement appears. Checkpoints inside the window are the Richmond Fed survey at 14:00 UTC, the Jefferson and Barkin remarks, and the 2-Year auction at 17:00 UTC, none of which is a Tier-1 print. Scores normalise back toward the low band after the 20:00 UTC close, with the Thursday Trump-Xi summit and Wednesday's 13:45 UTC flash PMI as the next scheduled catalysts and unresolved Iran headlines the main overnight gap mechanism.
